per_question.question: When converting line data to AFP, what information does a page definition control during composition?
per_question.answer:
## Page Definition Controls During Line Data to AFP Composition

When converting line data to AFP using RICOH ProcessDirector, the **page definition** controls the following characteristics during composition:

1. **The printable area of the page** — defines the boundaries within which content can be placed [aiw00o18.pdf, Page 1]

2. **The maximum number of lines that can print on a page** — sets the line capacity for each page [aiw00o18.pdf, Page 1]

3. **The beginning print position on the page** — determines where printing starts on the page [aiw00o18.pdf, Page 1]

4. **The printing direction** — controls whether printing goes across, up, or down the page [aiw00o18.pdf, Page 1]

5. **The page presentation** — specifies either portrait or landscape orientation [aiw00o18.pdf, Page 1]

6. **The fonts used to print each line of the page** — defines which fonts are applied to each line [aiw00o18.pdf, Page 1]

---

> **Note:** You can use one of the page definitions that RICOH ProcessDirector provides, or you can supply your own custom page definition [aiw00o18.pdf, Page 1].
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer lists all six page definition characteristics and the provided/own option, all directly supported by evidence [1].

per_question.question: If a customer sends a PDF 2.0 file through ProcessDirector with banner pages enabled, what happens to the file format?
per_question.answer:
## PDF 2.0 File Format Conversion with Banner Pages

When a customer sends a **PDF 2.0 file** through RICOH ProcessDirector with banner pages enabled, the following happens:

### What Occurs:

The PDF 2.0 file is **automatically converted to PDF 1.7 format**. This conversion is required because the banner page functionality depends on PDF 1.7 format. [aiw_pdfbanners.pdf, Page 1]

### Why This Happens:

PDF 1.7 is the format **required for the banner pages** to function correctly. ProcessDirector performs this conversion automatically as part of the banner page printing process. [aiw_ricohpdfptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

### This Behavior Applies Across Multiple Printer Types:

- **Ricoh PDF, TASKalfa, or Custom PDF printers** [aiw_ricohpdfptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]
- **Passthrough printers** [aiw_passthroughptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

### Key Takeaway for the Customer:

> ⚠️ If your workflow requires the output to remain in **PDF 2.0 format**, be aware that enabling banner pages will result in a **downconversion to PDF 1.7**. Plan accordingly if PDF 2.0 compliance is a requirement for downstream processes.

[aiw_pdfbanners.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer correctly states the PDF 2.0 to PDF 1.7 conversion and its reason, with only minor unstated-but-reasonable elaborations (automatic conversion, downstream compliance advice).

per_question.question: A job went into an error state and the printer threw an error — what's the likely cause and how do I fix it when working with character sets and code pages in AFP?
per_question.answer:
## AFP Error State: Character Set and Code Page Mismatch

### Likely Cause

The most probable cause of the job entering an error state and the printer throwing an error is a **mismatch between character names in the character set and code page**. Specifically, if the character names do not match between a character set and code page, the job goes into an error state in RICOH ProcessDirector and the printer issues an error. [modifyingtextstrings.pdf, Page 1] [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1] [insertingtext.pdf, Page 1] [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Fix It

Follow these steps to resolve the error:

1. **Identify the invalid pairing** — Determine which character set and code page combination was used when the error occurred. [modifyingtextstrings.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Change to a valid pair** — Update the character set and code page to a **valid, matching pair** where the character names align correctly. [modifyingtext.pdf, Page 1] [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 1]

3. **Reprocess the job** — Once the valid pair has been set, process the job again. [insertingtext.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Additional Things to Check

- **DBCS-coded fonts:** If you entered a code page that is part of a **Double-Byte Character Set (DBCS)-coded font**, you will see an error message advising you to use the **coded font name instead**. [modifyingtextstrings.pdf, Page 1] [vwb_CreateText.pdf, Page 1]

- **Display issues with text:** If text does not display correctly in RICOH Visual Workbench, consider changing the default code page via **Resources ⇒ Modify Default Encoding** (e.g., ASCII code page `IBM850 (GID=850)` or EBCDIC code page `IBM500 (GID=500)`). [openingafpfiles.pdf, Page 2]

- **File/cache errors:** If an error occurs when opening or working with a file, click **File ⇒ Reset** to close the file and clear cached resources from memory, then reopen the file. [openingafpfiles.pdf, Page 2]

---

> ⚠️ **Key Takeaway:** Always ensure your character set and code page are a **valid, compatible pair**. A mismatch is the primary trigger for this type of error in AFP processing.
per_question.judge_rationale: All claims trace to the retrieved passages (only the minor 'identify the invalid pairing' step is a light inference), and both key facts — mismatch cause and fix by valid pair plus reprocessing — are clearly conveyed.

per_question.question: When setting up a Kodak PDF printer for banner pages, what happens if the Header copies and Trailer copies job properties are set to 0, even if banner pages are enabled on the printer?
per_question.answer:
## Kodak PDF Printer: Effect of Setting Header/Trailer Copies to 0

When setting up a Kodak PDF printer for banner pages, if the **Header copies** and **Trailer copies** job properties are set to **0**, the printer will **not print a header page or a trailer page** for that specific job — even if banner pages are enabled on the printer.

As stated in the documentation:

> *"For header and trailer pages to print, the values of the Header copies and Trailer copies properties for the job must be set to 1 or greater. If the values of those job properties are set to 0, the printer does not print a header page or a trailer page for a specific job, even if these types of banner pages are enabled on the printer."*
[kdk_kodakpdfptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Takeaway

| Job Property | Value | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Header copies / Trailer copies | **1 or greater** | Banner pages **will** print |
| Header copies / Trailer copies | **0** | Banner pages **will NOT** print, regardless of printer settings |

---

### Recommendation

To ensure banner pages print correctly, make sure the **Header copies** and/or **Trailer copies** job properties are set to **1 or greater** at the job level, in addition to enabling banner pages on the printer itself. [kdk_kodakpdfptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately quotes the Kodak PDF printer documentation and conveys all key facts about copies set to 0 preventing banner pages despite printer-level enablement.

per_question.question: When setting up an inserter that doesn't produce any results files, what should I set the Completion method to, and why?
per_question.answer:
## Setting the Completion Method for an Inserter That Produces No Results Files

When setting up an inserter controller that does **not** produce any results files, you should set the **Completion method** to **Manual**. Here is a full explanation of what to configure and why:

---

### What to Set

**Completion method → Manual**

[CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Why Manual?

Because RICOH ProcessDirector relies on receiving a results file from the inserter controller to automatically detect when a job has finished insertion. If no results file is produced, RICOH ProcessDirector has no way to automatically determine when a job has completed insertion.

As stated in the documentation:

> *"If the inserter controller does not write results files... In the Completion method property on the General tab, select **Manual** because RICOH ProcessDirector cannot automatically determine when a job has finished insertion."*

[CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]

This is further confirmed by the general description of completion methods:

> *"Manual completion: An operator must select the Complete Insertion action to start the reconciliation process for the job. Use this method if the inserter controller does not create a job-specific results file after each job finishes insertion."*

[InserterCompletionMethods.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Additional Recommended Setting

You should also set the **Default insert status** property to **OK**. This ensures that on the Reconcile Job page, the operator only needs to manually mark the documents that require reprinting, rather than having to assess every document individually.

[CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Summary

1. Go to the **Administration** tab and navigate to **Devices → Inserter Controllers**. [CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
2. Open or create the relevant inserter controller.
3. On the **Results File tab**, clear the default values (since no results files are produced). [CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
4. On the **General tab**, set the **Completion method** property to **Manual**. [CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
5. On the **General tab**, set the **Default insert status** property to **OK**. [CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
6. Click **OK** and then **Enable** the inserter controller. [CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer correctly states Manual completion with accurate reasoning and the Default insert status OK detail, all directly supported by the retrieved evidence.

In the **Queue Name** field, you must type **`PASS`** [aiw00c_Define_PCLOut.pdf, Page 2].

per_question.question: When replacing POSTNET barcodes with IMBs in AFP Editor, how many total digits must the Mailer ID and Serial number fields combine to contain, and what happens if the Mailer ID value is shorter than expected?
per_question.answer:
## Replacing POSTNET Barcodes with IMBs in AFP Editor: Mailer ID & Serial Number Requirements

### Total Combined Digits

The Mailer ID and Serial number fields together **must combine to contain exactly 15 digits** in total. [barcode_IMBreplacedata_tab.pdf, Page 1]

This is confirmed across multiple sources: IMBs have two basic formats based on the Mailer ID length assigned by the USPS:

- **9-digit Mailer ID + 6-digit Serial Number = 15 digits**
- **6-digit Mailer ID + 9-digit Serial Number = 15 digits**

[vwb_barcodes_overview_imb_data.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What Happens if the Mailer ID Value is Shorter Than Expected?

If the value entered in the Mailer ID field is shorter than expected, **AFP Editor automatically adds leading zeroes** to the value so that the combined total of the Mailer ID and Serial number fields reaches the required **15 digits**. [barcode_IMBreplacedata_tab.pdf, Page 1]

> *"AFP Editor adds leading zeroes to the value in this field so that the value in the Mailer ID and Serial number fields together contain 15 digits."* [barcode_IMBreplacedata_tab.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Mailer ID Length | Serial Number Length | Combined Total |
|-----------------|---------------------|----------------|
| 9 digits | 6 digits | **15 digits** |
| 6 digits | 9 digits | **15 digits** |

[vwb_barcodes_overview_imb_data.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: Both key facts (15 combined digits and leading zeroes added to Mailer ID) are stated and directly supported by the retrieved evidence, including the 6/9-digit format pairings.

per_question.question: If I turn on a data collector but data collection itself is still disabled, will it start capturing anything?
per_question.answer:
## Data Collector Behavior When Data Collection Is Disabled

**Short answer: No, it will not capture anything.**

Even if you enable one or more individual data collectors, they will remain completely inactive if the overall data collection setting is turned off.

---

### Detailed Explanation

The behavior is explicitly documented as follows:

> **"If you enable one or more data collectors while data collection is disabled, the data collectors do nothing."**
> [reportsPostgresql_c_CaptureDataForPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]

This means there are **two separate conditions** that must both be true before any data is captured:

1. ✅ **Data collection must be globally enabled** (at the system/database settings level)
2. ✅ **The individual data collector(s) must also be enabled**

Only when **both** conditions are met will the data collectors begin capturing data when a triggering event occurs (e.g., a job enters a step, printing starts, or a printer status changes) [reportsPostgresql_c_CaptureDataForPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Summary Table

| Data Collection (Global) | Data Collector (Individual) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ❌ Disabled | ✅ Enabled | **Nothing captured** |
| ✅ Enabled | ❌ Disabled | **Nothing captured** |
| ✅ Enabled | ✅ Enabled | **Data captured** ✔️ |

---

### Recommendation

Make sure to enable data capturing in **Reports ⇒ Database Settings**, in addition to enabling each individual data collector you wish to use [aiw_supervisor.pdf, Page 1].
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately states collectors do nothing while data collection is disabled, cites the correct source, and mentions event-triggered capture, with only a minor inferred table row.

per_question.question: If I update the folder path on a repository that already has stored job history, does RICOH ProcessDirector automatically migrate the existing data to the new location?
per_question.answer:
## Migrating Existing Repository Data After a Folder Path Change

No, RICOH ProcessDirector does **not** automatically migrate existing data when you change the folder location of a repository.

### What the Documentation States

The documentation is explicit on this point:

> *"If you change the Folder location of a repository after jobs, documents, properties, or history information is stored, the data is not automatically moved to the new location. You must manually move the contents of the repository to the new location."*

[rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Steps to Change the Folder Location

If you still wish to proceed with changing the folder path, follow these steps:

1. Click the **Administration** tab. [rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]
2. In the left pane, click **Objects ⇒ Repositories**. [rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]
3. Select the repository whose folder location you want to change. [rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]
4. Click **Change Folder Location**. [rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]
5. Specify the new directory where you want the repository to store files or history information. [rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]
6. Click **OK**. [rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Important Manual Step Required

After completing the steps above, you **must manually move** all existing contents (jobs, documents, properties, and history information) from the old folder location to the new one. Failure to do so will result in previously stored data being inaccessible from the new location. [rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]

Additionally, note that if you do not specify a full path, the directory will be created in:
- **Linux:** `/var/aiw` directory
- **Windows:** `drive:\Program Files\Ricoh\ProcessDirector`

[rep_ChangeFolder.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: Answer accurately quotes the evidence, covers all key facts, with only a minor unstated inference about data inaccessibility.

per_question.question: When using a CopyToFolder step to send jobs to a printer hot folder, what functionality is lost compared to using a Passthrough printer?
per_question.answer:
## Functionality Lost When Using CopyToFolder vs. Passthrough Printer

When using a **CopyToFolder** step to send jobs to a printer hot folder, the following functionality is lost compared to using a **Passthrough printer**:

---

### 1. Cannot Use the "Schedule Jobs" Action

If you use the CopyToFolder step, you **cannot use the Schedule Jobs action** to assign jobs to a printer. The CopyToFolder step does not use the **Requested printer** property that the Schedule Jobs action sets to assign jobs to a printer. [aiw00o3.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 2. Cannot Send Job Properties (e.g., Number of Copies) to the Printer

When using the CopyToFolder step with a simple file copy command, **you cannot send the number of copies or other job properties to the printer**. These must be specified directly on the printer itself. [ip5khfippdsubmit.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Feature | Passthrough Printer | CopyToFolder Step |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule Jobs action | ✅ Supported | ❌ Not supported |
| Send job properties (e.g., copies) to printer | ✅ Supported | ❌ Not supported |
| Copy job to hot folder | ✅ Supported | ✅ Supported |

---

In contrast, a **Passthrough printer device** uses its **Printer command property** to copy the job into a hot folder associated with the printer, while also maintaining integration with job scheduling and printer load balancing features. [aiw_jobtype_for_printing.pdf, Page 1]

per_question.question: What's the difference between a Kodak PDF printer device and a Passthrough printer device, and which one should I use if my printer model is supported by both?

## Difference Between Kodak PDF Printer and Passthrough Printer Devices

### What They Have in Common
Both **Kodak PDF printer devices** and **Passthrough printer devices** can print jobs in **PDF or PostScript format** [kdk_c_Define_KodakPDF.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Key Differences

| Feature | Kodak PDF Printer | Passthrough Printer |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary function** | Prints PDF files, including jobs converted to PDF format; sends PDF with inserted KDK commands [aiw_jobtype_for_printing.pdf, Page 1] | Usually prints data streams such as PostScript, PDF, and PCL **without** file conversion [aiw00c4.pdf, Page 1] |

## What an Inserter Controller Object Defines and Controls in RICOH ProcessDirector

An inserter controller object in RICOH ProcessDirector represents the inserter controller software running on another computer (such as a Windows computer), which can manage several inserter devices that insert printed documents and additional materials (such as marketing materials) into envelopes [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Core Purpose

The inserter controller object controls **how RICOH ProcessDirector communicates with the inserter controller** and **how it reprints documents after insertion** [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Specifically, the Inserter Controller Object Defines:

1. **Scripts/Commands for Communication**
   - The script or command for **sending control files** to the inserter controller
   - The script for **receiving results files** from the inserter controller
   [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Rules for Control and Results Files**
   - The rules for **writing control files** (governing how insertion instructions are formatted and sent)
   - The rules for **interpreting results files** (governing how insertion outcomes are read back)
   [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1]

3. **Default Insert Status**
   - The default insert status assigned to documents that have **no reported status** in the results file
   [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1]

4. **Completion Method**
   - How RICOH ProcessDirector **determines when the inserter controller has finished inserting a job**
   [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1]

5. **Reprint Method**
   - The method used for **reprinting documents that were damaged during insertion** (open-loop or closed-loop)
   [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1] [DefiningInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Additional Configuration Details Governed by the Object

When creating or modifying an inserter controller object, the following settings are also configured depending on your environment:

- **Control file format**: Fixed-length record (FLR), comma-delimited (DEL), or XML [DefiningInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
- **Encoding** (for FLR format): ASCII or UTF-8 [DefiningInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
- **Whether a header record is required** in the control file [DefiningInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
- **Whether results files are job-specific** (one per job) or non-job-specific (e.g., Gunther-style, requiring a polling command) [CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]
- **Receive vs. Polling command** for results files, depending on whether results are job-specific [CreatingInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What It Governs at the Job Level

Once associated with a job, RICOH ProcessDirector uses the inserter controller object to:

- **Write the inserter control file** for the job and send it to the inserter controller
- **Receive the inserter results file** for the job from the inserter controller and interpret it

[AssociatingInserterControllersWithJobs.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Flexibility Note

You can create **more than one inserter controller object** to represent a single physical inserter controller — this allows you to specify **different properties for different jobs or applications** without changing the underlying hardware setup [InserterControllerObject.pdf, Page 1] [DefiningInserterControllers.pdf, Page 1].

per_question.question: We're using a third-party program to modify PDF content during workflow processing, and now IdentifyPDFDocuments is giving wrong results. What's the rule about where in the workflow that modification step needs to go?
per_question.answer:
## Rule for Third-Party PDF Modification Steps in Workflows

This is a well-documented requirement. Here is the clear rule and the reasoning behind it:

---

### ✅ The Rule

**Any step that calls a third-party program to modify PDF content MUST be placed BEFORE the `IdentifyPDFDocuments` step in the workflow — never after it.**

> *"If those or other programs that change the PDF data process your production PDF files, ensure that the steps calling those programs occur **before** the IdentifyPDFDocuments step."*
> [pdfw_i_c_stepschangedata.pdf, Page 1]

This is also confirmed in the step configuration documentation:

> *"If you add an IdentifyPDFDocuments step to a workflow, place the step **after all steps that alter the PDF file**. If you add the step before a step that alters the file, **unexpected results can occur**."*
> [pdfw_t_configuringidentstep.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Why This Matters

Operations that alter data in a PDF file can cause the control files built with the **RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat** to not function as expected. [pdfw_i_c_stepschangedata.pdf, Page 1]

This means the document property definitions and page grouping rules embedded in the `.ctl` control file may no longer align correctly with the modified PDF content if `IdentifyPDFDocuments` runs first.

---

### 🔧 Recommended Corrective Action

1. **Reorder your workflow** so that your third-party PDF modification step comes **before** the `IdentifyPDFDocuments` step.
2. **Run a test** of your workflow using the same sample PDF file that was used to create the control file in the RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat. [pdfw_i_c_stepschangedata.pdf, Page 1]
3. If you are processing **PDF 2.0 files** and still get unexpected results after reordering, do one of the following:
   - Update the control file using **RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat version 3.6 or above**, and copy it to the correct location. [pdfw_t_configuringidentstep.pdf, Page 1]
   - Place a step based on the **`OptimizePDF` step template** in the workflow **before** the `IdentifyPDFDocuments` step. [pdfw_t_configuringidentstep.pdf, Page 1] [pdfw_i_c_stepschangedata.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Workflow Order

```
[Third-Party PDF Modification Step]
        ↓
[OptimizePDF step] ← (if needed for PDF 2.0 issues)
        ↓
[IdentifyPDFDocuments step]
```
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately states the ordering rule, the control-file caveat, and the PDF 2.0 remedies with correct citations; only minor paraphrase drift on the plug-in version wording.

per_question.question: When a job is made up of multiple input files, which workflow does the parent job use versus the child jobs on an input device?
per_question.answer:
## Parent Job vs. Child Job Workflows on an Input Device

When a job is made up of multiple input files, RICOH ProcessDirector uses **different workflows for the parent job and the child jobs**. Here is how they are assigned:

---

### Parent Job Workflow

The **parent job** uses the **`ParentNoPrint`** workflow.

This is set via the **Workflow** property on the input device. [aiw00c12.pdf, Page 1]

This is consistent across multiple batching scenarios — for example, when using the **Batch** batching method, the input device property **Workflow** must be set to **`ParentNoPrint`**. [aiw_sdk_batch.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Child Job Workflow

The **child jobs** use the workflow specified in the **Child workflow** property on the input device. [aiw00c12.pdf, Page 1]

This child workflow is the one you create or configure to handle the actual processing of each individual input file. If grouping behavior is needed (e.g., waiting for all child jobs before proceeding), the child workflow should include a step based on the **`WaitForGroup`** step template. [aiw00c12.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Job Type | Workflow Used |
|---|---|
| **Parent Job** | `ParentNoPrint` (set via the **Workflow** property) |
| **Child Jobs** | The workflow set in the **Child workflow** property |

---

### Additional Configuration Notes

- The **Submit step** property on the input device must be set to **`SubmitInputFiles`**, which is the step responsible for creating the child jobs and assigning each one a process group ID and position number within the group. [aiw00c12.pdf, Page 1]
- For **Hot folder** input devices, the **Batching method** property must also be set to a value other than **None**. [aiw00c12.pdf, Page 1]
- For **LPD input devices with a Linux parent server**, note that parent jobs with multiple children **cannot** be created — instead, one parent job and one child job are created per input file. [aiw00c12.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately reflects the evidence that the parent job uses the Workflow property (ParentNoPrint) and child jobs use the Child workflow property, with supporting details all traceable to the retrieved documents.

per_question.question: Which printer types in ProcessDirector can report back job status while printing, and how does it handle status monitoring for Passthrough and PCLOut printers?
per_question.answer:
# Printer Status Reporting in RICOH ProcessDirector

## Printers That Can Report Job Status While Printing

RICOH ProcessDirector can get status on the job **while it is printing** by communicating directly with the following printer types:

- **AFP printers** (IPDS format, requires AFP Support feature)
- **Ricoh PDF printers**

[aiw00c4.pdf, Page 1]

Specifically for AFP printers, RICOH ProcessDirector can:
- Receive status information about the job from those printers
- Send requests to the printer, including **interrupting a job** that is currently printing
- Use the **Jump to action** to move to a different place in the job and resume printing

[aiw00o3.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Status Monitoring for Passthrough Printers

For **Passthrough printers**, RICOH ProcessDirector handles status monitoring as follows:

- It **runs a command** that is defined for the printer and **monitors the response** to that command [aiw00c4.pdf, Page 1]
- However, it **cannot report the status of the job** that it sent [aiw00c4.pdf, Page 1] [aiw00c4pass.pdf, Page 1]
- It can send requests to the **software queue** that represents the printer, but **not to the printer itself** [aiw00o3.pdf, Page 1]
- If a Passthrough printer is configured to copy jobs to a **hot folder**, RICOH ProcessDirector **cannot receive status information** about the job from the printer [aiw00o3.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Status Monitoring for PCLOut Printers

For **PCLOut printers**, the behavior is identical in terms of limitations:

- RICOH ProcessDirector **runs a command** defined for the printer and **monitors the response** to that command [aiw00c4.pdf, Page 1]
- It **cannot report the status of the job** that it sent [aiw00c4.pdf, Page 1]
- It **cannot receive status information** about the job from those printers [aiw00o3.pdf, Page 1]

---

## Summary Table

| Printer Type | Reports Job Status While Printing? | Monitoring Method |
|---|---|---|
| AFP Printer | ✅ Yes | Direct communication with printer |
| Ricoh PDF Printer | ✅ Yes | Direct communication with printer |
| Passthrough Printer | ❌ No | Runs a command; monitors response only |
| PCLOut Printer | ❌ No | Runs a command; monitors response only |

[aiw00c4.pdf, Page 1] [aiw00o3.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: Every claim traces directly to the retrieved passages and all three key facts are conveyed accurately with correct citations.

Therefore, if your workflow depends on document properties being populated from index tags in the AFP file, you **must** point the IdentifyDocuments step to the appropriate `.ctl` control file created by RICOH Visual Workbench. [configuringidentifystep3.pdf, Page 1]

## Placement and Function of the `SetPropertiesForReconcile` Step in Manual Reconciliation

### Where to Place the Step

The `SetPropertiesForReconcile` step must be placed in **two specific locations** within the workflow:

---

#### **Location 1 — Main Branch (Primary Placement)**

Place the step based on `SetPropertiesForReconcile`:

1. **After** the `WriteDocumentsToDatabase` step, **AND**
2. **After** any step that changes the position of documents in the job, **AND**
3. **Before** the `BuildPDFFromDocuments` or `BuildAFPFromDocuments` step.

[doc_c_SetUpManualReconciliation.pdf, Page 1]

---

#### **Location 2 — Reprint Branch (Optional, if processing child reprint jobs in the same workflow)**

If you add a branch to handle reprint child jobs within the same workflow, the step must also be placed:

1. After a `SetDocPropsFromConditions` step,
2. After the `UpdateDocumentsInDatabase` step,
3. And then **connected** to the step that follows `BuildPDFFromDocuments` or `BuildAFPFromDocuments` in the original branch (e.g., the `CountPages` step).

[doc_c_SetUpManualReconciliation.pdf, Page 2]

---

### What the `SetPropertiesForReconcile` Step Actually Does

The `SetPropertiesForReconcile` step performs the following function:

> **It sets the *Insert sequence* property for each document in a job.**

Once this value is set, the operator can use it on the **Reconcile Job dialog** to locate specific documents during reconciliation. Specifically, the operator can:

- Select **"By range"** on the Reconcile Job dialog and specify a range of Insert sequence values, **OR**
- Select **"By properties"** and specify a particular Insert sequence value.

[doc_c_SetUpManualReconciliation.pdf, Page 1]

This capability is also confirmed more broadly in the feature overview, which states that the step *"lets you use the Insert sequence document property to find documents on the Reconcile Job dialog or the Documents portlet."* [aiw_o_pdfdocsupport_featov.pdf, Page 1]

---

| Primary placement | After `WriteDocumentsToDatabase`, before `BuildPDFFromDocuments`/`BuildAFPFromDocuments` | [doc_c_SetUpManualReconciliation.pdf, Page 1] |
| Reprint branch placement | After `UpdateDocumentsInDatabase`, connected back to main branch | [doc_c_SetUpManualReconciliation.pdf, Page 2] |

per_question.question: When using the Number batching method for a hot folder input device, what workflow should be set and what determines whether files are submitted as child jobs versus a single ZIP job?

## Number Batching Method – Workflow Configuration & Job Submission Behavior

### Required Workflow Setting

When using the **Number** batching method for a hot folder input device, you must set the following input device properties:

- **Workflow:** `ParentNoPrint` [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1]
- **Child workflow:** The workflow that is appropriate for the print files in the job [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1]
- **Submit step:** `SubmitInputFiles` [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What Determines Child Jobs vs. a Single ZIP Job

The **"Create .zip file"** property controls how files are submitted:

| Setting | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Yes** | All input files matching the **Data patterns** property are combined into a single ZIP file and submitted as **one single job** [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1] |
| **No** | All input files are submitted as **child jobs** [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1] |

This is further confirmed in the batch job setup documentation: *"If this property is set to Yes, all input files that match the value set in the Data Patterns property are combined as a .zip file and submitted as a single job. If this property is set to No, all input files are submitted as child jobs."* [aiw00cbatchfolder.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Additional Relevant Properties

- **Number of files to batch:** Defines how many files the hot folder waits to receive before submitting them as a single group [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1]
- **Data patterns:** A regular expression pattern that matches file names to be counted and submitted. The default value is `.*$`, which matches all file names [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1]

> **Note:** Only files whose names match the **Data patterns** property are counted toward the batch total. [aiw_sdk_number.pdf, Page 1]

## Purpose of Pipeline Manager in RICOH Visual Workbench

### Overview

**Pipeline Manager** is a mode of RICOH Visual Workbench designed to let you configure and run a set of filters, in a specific order, to **process large AFP files quickly and efficiently** [vwb_PipelineMgrOverview.pdf, Page 1].

---

### What It Allows You to Do with AFP Files

Pipeline Manager enables you to **pre-process AFP files** by chaining together filters from multiple modes and plug-ins into a single, streamlined process [vwb_PipelineMgrOverview.pdf, Page 1]. Specifically, it allows you to:

- **Generate page groups and indexes** (using AFP Indexer filters)
- **Add bar codes** (using AFP Enhancer filters)
- **Write the resulting AFP file** — all within **one single process**
- The input AFP is **read once**, and the output AFP is **written once**, making it highly efficient [vwb_PipelineMgrOverview.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Available Filters

Pipeline Manager draws filters from the following modes and plug-ins:

- **AFP Indexer** — has filters available
- **AFP Enhancer** — has filters available
- **AFP Editor** — has filters available (if installed)
- **Whitespace Manager** — has filters available (if installed) [vwb_PipelineMgrOverview.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Configure and Run a Pipeline

1. Open a sample AFP file in RICOH Visual Workbench
2. If the file does not contain page groups, use AFP Indexer to create them
3. Click **Mode ⇒ Pipeline Manager**
4. Click **Tools ⇒ Manage Pipeline**
5. Add filters from the **Available Pipeline Elements** list to the **Current Pipeline Definition** list
6. Configure any required filter parameters
7. Arrange filters in the correct order (filters run **top to bottom**)
8. Click **Apply** to save your changes [vwb_ManagePipeline.pdf, Page 1]

> ⚠️ **Important:** The order of filters matters. For example, running filters such as *Indexer* and *Remove Page Groups* in a different order can produce different results [vwb_ManagePipeline.pdf, Page 1].
per_question.judge_rationale: All claims trace to the retrieved documents with only minor inferential attribution of specific filters to modes; both key facts are conveyed clearly.

per_question.answer:

per_question.question: When setting up a Custom PDF printer in ProcessDirector for a PostScript printer not on the supported Ricoh list, what file do I need to get before I can create the printer object, and where do I get it?
per_question.answer:
## File Required Before Creating a Custom PDF Printer Object

Before you can create a Custom PDF printer object in RICOH ProcessDirector for a PostScript printer not on the supported Ricoh list, you need a **custom printer definition file**.

### What is it?

The custom printer definition file is a special file that lets RICOH ProcessDirector create device-specific PostScript for your printer. It is created by Ricoh based on the PostScript Printer Description (PPD) file supplied by the printer's manufacturer. RICOH ProcessDirector supports custom printer definition files with **GPZ and ZIP extensions**. [aiw_c_DefineCustomPrinterDevice.pdf, Page 1]

### Where do you get it?

You must **contact your Ricoh support representative** to obtain this file. Specifically:

1. **Talk to your Ricoh support representative** about your PostScript printer before defining the Custom PDF printer. [aiw_c_DefineCustomPrinter.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Your Ricoh support representative will send you** the custom printer definition file. [aiw_c_DefineCustomPrinter.pdf, Page 1]

### What do you do once you have it?

Once you receive the file, you **import it into RICOH ProcessDirector**, which then installs it on the printer server. Only after that can you proceed to define the Custom PDF printer object. [aiw_c_ImportCustomPrinterFile.pdf, Page 1]

The import steps are:
1. Click the **Administration** tab.
2. In the left pane, click **Devices ⇒ Printers**.
3. Click **Add ⇒ Custom PDF Printer**.
4. On the General tab, select the printer server, then click **Import file**.
5. On the RICOH Printer Connector page, click **Import Custom Printer Definition File**.
6. Navigate to and select the file — RICOH ProcessDirector will install it on the printer server. [aiw_c_ImportCustomPrinterFile.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: All claims (custom printer definition file, from Ricoh support representative, device-specific PostScript, GPZ/ZIP, import steps) are directly supported by the evidence, and all key facts are conveyed.

per_question.question: When editing AFP banner page control files to include barcodes, which fields in the barcode line format are optional and can be left out?
per_question.answer:
## Optional Fields in AFP Banner Page Barcode Line Format

Based on the documentation, here is the answer to your question:

When editing AFP banner page control files to add barcode entries, the barcode line uses the following format:

```
FieldX FieldName;FieldType;[key];;;InchesFromLeft;InchesFromTop;Rotation;BarcodeType;Height;Modifier;Asterisk;HRI;ModuleWidth;WideNarrowRatio;RowSize;NumberOfRows
```

[aiw00bannerbcode.pdf, Page 1]

### Optional Fields

The documentation explicitly states:

> *"You cannot omit any of the fields **except** the ModuleWidth, WideNarrowRatio, RowSize, and NumberOfRows fields."*

[aiw00bannerbcode.pdf, Page 1]

Therefore, the **four optional fields** that can be left out are:

| # | Optional Field |
|---|----------------|
| 1 | **ModuleWidth** |
| 2 | **WideNarrowRatio** |
| 3 | **RowSize** |
| 4 | **NumberOfRows** |

### Practical Example

You can see these optional fields left empty (trailing semicolons with no values) in the sample entries provided in the documentation:

```
Field2 Barcode;JobTicketField;[JobID];;;2.25;1.0;0;3of9;0.625;1;no;none;;;;
Field100 Barcode2;JobTicketField;[Job.ID.Value];;;0.950;8.35;0;3of9;0.625;1;no;below;;;;;
```

[aiw00bannerbcode.pdf, Page 1]

> ⚠️ **Important Note:** All other fields in the line are **mandatory** and cannot be omitted. Also, remember that all fields are separated by semicolons (`;`), even when the optional fields are left blank. [aiw00bannerbcode.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately quotes the evidence, listing the four omissible fields, noting all others are required and fields are semicolon-separated.

per_question.question: What dot gain percentage does the 'Accutone' appearance value compensate for on a 50% dot when using generic tone transfer curve CMRs in AFP color management?
per_question.answer:
## Accutone Dot Gain Compensation

Based on the documentation provided, the **'Accutone'** appearance value compensates for a dot gain of **22%** on a 50% dot when using generic tone transfer curve CMRs in AFP color management.

Specifically, the documentation states:

> *"Accutone — The output is adjusted to show a dot gain of 22% for a 50% dot."*

[cac_CMRToneTransfer.pdf, Page 1]

### Context: All Generic Tone Transfer Curve Appearance Values

For reference, here is the full list of appearance values and their corresponding dot gain adjustments on a 50% dot:

| Appearance Value | Dot Gain on 50% Dot |
|---|---|
| **Dark** | 33% |
| **Accutone** | **22%** |
| **Highlight Midtone** | 14% |
| **Standard** | Counteracts dot gain entirely |

[cac_CMRToneTransfer.pdf, Page 1]

> **Note:** The **Standard** appearance value is unique in that it is adjusted *just enough* to effectively counteract the dot gain, rather than targeting a specific percentage. [cac_CMRToneTransfer.pdf, Page 1]

per_question.question: When working with AFP files, do I need to link custom document properties to index tags if I only want to split a job based on the number of sheets per document?
per_question.answer:
## Answer

No, you do not need to link custom document properties to index tags if your only goal is to split a job based on the number of sheets per document.

This is explicitly stated in the documentation:

> *"If you want to manipulate documents or jobs using only the standard properties provided in all document processing features — for example, if you want to split a job based on the number of sheets in each document — you do not need to link custom document properties to index tags."*
[designingproperties.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Additional Context

Linking custom document properties to index tags becomes necessary when you want to use **custom properties** for more advanced operations. For example:

- If you have a custom document property representing a **postal code** and you want to **sort, split, or group documents by postal code**, then you would need to link that custom property to its corresponding index tag. [designingproperties.pdf, Page 1]
- When a property *is* linked to an index tag, RICOH ProcessDirector steps assign the value of the index tag in a production AFP file to the property in the workflow. [linkingproperties.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary

| Use Case | Link Custom Properties to Index Tags? |
|---|---|
| Split job by number of sheets per document | ❌ Not required |
| Sort/split/group by custom property (e.g., postal code) | ✅ Required |

So for your specific scenario — splitting based on sheet count — you can proceed using the standard properties without any additional configuration in Document Property Designer. [designingproperties.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: Correctly answers 'no' with direct citation and covers when linking is needed, but omits that index tags are also called Tagged Logical Elements (TLEs).

per_question.question: When using the Pages batching method, what happens if a single PDF file has more pages than the configured batch threshold and the 'Exceed pages to batch' setting is turned off?
per_question.answer:
## Pages Batching Method: Single File Exceeding Threshold with 'Exceed Pages to Batch' Set to No

When using the **Pages batching method**, if a single PDF file contains more pages than the value configured for the **Number of pages to batch** property, and the **Exceed pages to batch** property is set to **No**, the following occurs:

---

### ⚠️ The File Cannot Be Submitted

The file is **blocked from being submitted**, and **processing for the hot folder or SFTP input device stops entirely** [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1].

---

### 🔄 How to Resolve the Situation

Processing will remain halted until **one of the following corrective actions** is taken:

1. **Delete the input file** from the hot folder or SFTP input device, removing the problematic file entirely [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1].

2. **Increase the "Number of pages to batch" value** to at least the number of pages contained in the file, so the file no longer exceeds the threshold [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1].

3. **Change the "Exceed pages to batch" property to Yes**, which will then allow the oversized file to be submitted — either as part of a batch with other waiting PDF files, or as a batch containing only that single file [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1].

---

### 📋 Summary Table

| Setting | Result |
|---|---|
| Exceed pages to batch = **Yes** | File is submitted (alone or with other files) |
| Exceed pages to batch = **No** | File is **blocked**; input device processing **stops** |

---

> **Important Note:** The Pages batching method does not support encrypted or password-protected PDF files. If such a file is submitted, RICOH ProcessDirector will issue an error message because it cannot open the file to count its pages [aiw_sdk_pages.pdf, Page 1].
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately reflects evidence [1]/[4], stating the file cannot be submitted, processing stops, and listing the three remedies.

per_question.question: When using IBM DB2 as the main database and wanting to use the built-in PostgreSQL for Reports, what extra software do I need to install on the primary computer?
per_question.answer:
## Extra Software Required: Docker Engine

When using **IBM DB2 as the main database** and wanting to use the **built-in PostgreSQL for the Reports feature**, you need to install **Docker Engine** on your primary computer.

This is required because the PostgreSQL database provided with RICOH ProcessDirector is packaged and runs inside a **Docker container**. [reportsPostgresql_c_SetUpRPDconnectToPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]

### Key Details:

- However, since that PostgreSQL runs in a Docker container, **Docker Engine must be installed on the primary computer** for it to function. [reportsPostgresql_c_SetUpRPDconnectToPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]
- This is also consistent with the general PostgreSQL database configuration requirement: *"The PostgreSQL database is installed in a Docker container, so Docker Engine must be installed on the primary computer."* [aiwi_whatsnew.pdf, Page 3]

---

### Alternative (if you prefer NOT to install Docker Engine):

If you do not want to install Docker Engine, you have the option to **install your own independent PostgreSQL instance** — either on the primary computer or on another computer in your network — and connect RICOH ProcessDirector to that instead. [reportsPostgresql_c_SetUpRPDconnectToPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]

> ⚠️ **Note:** If you install an independent PostgreSQL on the primary computer, do **not** set the server address to `localhost` — use the **IP address** of the primary computer instead. [reportsPostgresql_c_SetUpRPDconnectToPostgreSQL.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer correctly states Docker Engine is required because the bundled PostgreSQL runs in a Docker container, and all supplementary details (alternative independent PostgreSQL, non-localhost note) are directly supported by the retrieved evidence.

per_question.question: When a JDF job ticket uses absolute path names for files, how does RICOH ProcessDirector locate those files, and where is the configuration stored that maps those paths?
per_question.answer:
## How RICOH ProcessDirector Locates Files Using Absolute Path Names in JDF Job Tickets

When a JDF job ticket uses absolute path names to reference files, RICOH ProcessDirector follows a specific process to locate those files. Here is a detailed explanation:

---

### How the File Location Process Works

1. **Absolute paths allow files to be anywhere on the network.**
Files listed with absolute path names can be located anywhere on your network that is accessible from the RICOH ProcessDirector primary server — they are not restricted to the hot folder location. [aiw_sdk_fileloc.pdf, Page 1]

2. **RICOH ProcessDirector uses a mapping file.**
When absolute path names are used, RICOH ProcessDirector uses the absolute path statements **in conjunction with a mapping file** to find the files. The mapping file matches the file paths listed in the job ticket to file paths on mounted file systems. [aiw_sdk_fileloc.pdf, Page 1]

3. **The search sequence is as follows:**
- RICOH ProcessDirector looks through **each location listed in the mapping file** until it finds the files.
- If it reaches the end of the mapping file without finding the files, it then looks in the **Folder location** of the hot folder input device.
- If the files are still not found, it **waits and checks again at the next poll interval**. [aiw_sdk_fileloc.pdf, Page 1]

4. **Once found, files are copied to the hot folder.**
Regardless of where the files are found, RICOH ProcessDirector copies them into the location specified in the **Folder location** property of the hot folder input device before processing the job. [aiw_sdk_fileloc.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Supported Absolute Path Name Formats

The recommended format is:
```
file://hostname/drive:/dir/filename
```
*(Omit `drive:` for systems that do not use drive letters.)*

Supported but **not recommended** formats include:
```
file:///drive:\dir\filename
file://drive:/dir/filename
file://drive:\dir\filename
drive:\dir\filename
drive:/dir/filename
```
[aiw_sdk_fileloc.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Where the Mapping File Configuration Is Stored

- **Sample file location:** RICOH ProcessDirector provides a sample mapping file called `system_map.cfg` located at:
`/aiw/aiw1/samples/config/` [aiw00csysmap.pdf, Page 1]

- **Active configuration file location:** You must copy and customize the file, placing it in:
`/aiw/aiw1/control_files/config/` [aiw00csysmap.pdf, Page 1]

- **Only one mapping file is needed** per primary server, and it can list as many file paths as required. [aiw_sdk_fileloc.pdf, Page 1]

---

### How to Configure the Mapping File in the System

Follow these steps to specify the mapping file:

1. Click the **Administration** tab.
2. In the left pane, click **Settings ⇒ System**.
3. In the **File system mapping file** field, type the file path of your mapping file.
4. Click **SAVE**.

> ✅ You do **not** need to restart the system after saving. [aiw00csysmap.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: All claims trace directly to the evidence and the answer covers the mapping-file mechanism, search order, and configuration location, though it only implicitly states the mapping file resides on the primary server.

per_question.question: A customer has InfoPrint 4100 printers and wants to add agent photos to letterhead but the black and white images look too dark and flat. What specific hardware/software upgrades does Ricoh recommend to get better grayscale image quality on those printers?
per_question.answer:
## Ricoh Recommendations for Improving Grayscale Image Quality on InfoPrint 4100 Printers

Based on the scenario you've described — adding agent photos to letterhead where the black and white images appear too dark and flat — Ricoh recommends the following specific hardware and software upgrades:

---

### Step 1: Upgrade the Print Controller

**Upgrade the printer to use a controller with the InfoPrint POWER architecture running microcode release 15.4 or later.**

This is the foundational upgrade. It adds support for the AFP color management architecture, which enables high-quality grayscale printing using **halftones** and **tone transfer curves**. Without this, the advanced grayscale capabilities are not available. [cac_Halftone_4100.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 2: Purchase and Install the AFP Color Emulation Feature

**Install the AFP Color Emulation feature on the upgraded printer controller.**

This feature is required to print color objects (such as agent photographs, which are typically JPEG, TIFF, GIF, or IOCA images) in high-quality grayscale. Specifically, once installed, AFP Color Management lets you natively print **GIF, IOCA FS11, IOCA FS45, JPEG, and TIFF images** in high-quality grayscale. [cac_IP4100.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 3: Install and Use AFP Resource Installer

**Install AFP Resource Installer to manage the images.**

This software tool is used to:
- Install the agent photographs into a **resource library**
- Associate the images with the appropriate **halftone CMRs** and **tone transfer curve CMRs** to achieve the best quality output
- Assign the images names that print jobs can reference [cac_Halftone_4100.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step 4: Configure CMRs Appropriately

**Select and apply the correct Color Management Resources (CMRs).**

Choose the appropriate **generic halftone** and **tone transfer curve CMRs** for the InfoPrint 4100 based on the desired **line screen frequency** and **appearance values**. Then associate the agent photographs with those CMRs in the resource library. [cac_Halftone_4100.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Step 5: Update InfoPrint Manager Destinations

**Reconfigure RICOH InfoPrint Manager** so that print jobs containing photographs are routed specifically to the printer line that has the AFP Color Emulation feature installed. [cac_Halftone_4100.pdf, Page 2]

---

### Optional Step 6: Consider the Image Enhancement Feature (for MS1, MD1, MD2 Models)

For **InfoPrint 4100 Models MS1, MD1, and MD2** specifically, Ricoh also offers the **Image Enhancement feature**, which provides:
- **Enhanced fusing technology** to minimize toner distortion
- **Optimized developer unit** for high coverage and high-density applications
- **Improved halftones** tailored to new hardware and toner technology

This can deliver **even better image quality** beyond what the AFP Color Emulation feature alone provides. [cac_IP4100.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Upgrade | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| InfoPrint POWER architecture + Microcode 15.4+ | Hardware/Firmware | Enables AFP color management & grayscale support |
| AFP Color Emulation Feature | Software/Feature | Enables high-quality grayscale printing of photos (JPEG, TIFF, etc.) |
| AFP Resource Installer | Software | Manages images and associates CMRs |
| Halftone & Tone Transfer Curve CMRs | Resources | Controls gray shading and tonal range |
| Image Enhancement Feature (MS1/MD1/MD2 only) | Hardware | Further improves fusing, halftones, and density |
per_question.judge_rationale: All recommended upgrades trace directly to the retrieved evidence with only minor benign inference (image formats of agent photos), and all three key facts are conveyed.

per_question.question: When using the Time batching method, what happens to files that were already sitting in the hot folder before the configured start date and time kicks in?
per_question.answer:
## Files Pre-existing in the Hot Folder Before the Configured Start Date/Time

When using the **Time batching method**, files that already exist in the hot folder or SFTP input device **before** the configured start date and time are **not ignored or discarded**. Here is what happens:

---

### What Happens to Pre-existing Files

Those files **will be included in the first batch** submitted by the input device once the configured start date and time is reached.

> **Note:** *"If files exist in the hot folder or SFTP input device prior to the initial date and time set in the Batching start date and Batching start time properties, those files will be included in the first batch submitted by the input device."* [aiw_sdk_time.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Step-by-Step Summary

1. You configure the **Batching start date** and **Batching start time** on the input device. [aiw_sdk_time.pdf, Page 1]
2. The hot folder or SFTP input device **waits** until that specified date and time before it begins submitting batches. [aiw_sdk_time.pdf, Page 1]
3. Any files that were **already sitting in the hot folder** before that start date/time are **picked up and included** in the very **first batch** that is submitted. [aiw_sdk_time.pdf, Page 1]
4. Files are printed in the order specified by their **Last modified timestamp**. [aiw_sdk_time.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Key Takeaway

Pre-existing files are **not lost or skipped** — they are simply held until the batching method activates, at which point they become part of the first submission. This ensures no files are inadvertently missed when the Time batching method first kicks in. [aiw_sdk_time.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately quotes the evidence that pre-existing files are included in the first batch, but omits the second key fact about the time zone handling of the Batching start time.

per_question.question: When using a PCLOut printer, does it save AFP resources like fonts or overlays from one job so they can be reused in the next job?
per_question.answer:
## PCLOut Printer: AFP Resource Saving Between Jobs

**No**, a PCLOut printer does **not** save AFP resources from one job for reuse in the next job.

This is explicitly stated in the documentation:

> *"PCLOut printers convert jobs on a **job-by-job basis**. They do **not** create and save AFP resources (such as fonts, overlays, or page segments) from previous jobs."*
> [aiw00c_PCLOutLimitations.pdf, Page 1]

### Specific Limitations Regarding Resource Reuse

The documentation further lists this as an explicit unsupported capability:

- ❌ **Using any printer-resident resources** [aiw00c_PCLOutLimitations.pdf, Page 1]
- ❌ **Reusing printer resources (including fonts) from one job to the next** [aiw00c_PCLOutLimitations.pdf, Page 1]

### Additional Note on Overlays and Page Segments

Even within a single job, there is a processing concern: if print jobs include **page overlays or page segments**, they are rendered **after all other objects are processed**, which may cause issues when the order of overlapping objects is critical. [aiw00c_PCLOutLimitations.pdf, Page 1]

### Summary

Every job sent to a PCLOut printer is processed completely independently. Resources such as fonts, overlays, and page segments must be available for **each individual job** — there is no cross-job resource caching or reuse capability with PCLOut printers. [aiw00c_PCLOutLimitations.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer directly quotes the evidence, conveys all three key facts, and adds only supported details about overlay rendering order.

per_question.question: What tools do I use to define page groups for PDF versus AFP files when setting up jobs for an inserter?
per_question.answer:
## Tools for Defining Page Groups: PDF vs. AFP Files

The tools you use differ depending on the file type:

---

### 📄 For PDF Files
You use **RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat** to define page groups.

**Steps to define a page group in a PDF file:**
1. Open a PDF file in **Adobe Acrobat Professional** and click **Ricoh ⇒ Select** to make the plug-in the active tool. [tt_c_EnhancePDFVerification.pdf, Page 1]
2. Draw a box around the text you want to use to define text-based page groups, or draw a box anywhere to define page groups that are not based on text. [tt_c_EnhancePDFVerification.pdf, Page 1]
3. Click **Define Page Group**. You can define a page group based on text that appears repeatedly throughout the PDF file, or based on a fixed number of pages. [tt_c_EnhancePDFVerification.pdf, Page 1]
4. Follow the instructions for defining a page group in the plug-in help system or in *RICOH ProcessDirector: Using RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat*. [tt_c_EnhancePDFVerification.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 🖨️ For AFP Files
You use **RICOH Visual Workbench** (specifically its **AFP Indexer** component) to define page groups.

AFP Indexer can create page groups in the following ways:
- **Fixed-length page groups** — each page group contains a set number of pages. [pagegroups_overview.pdf, Page 1]
- **Trigger-based page groups** — a trigger is a block of text occurring in a consistent location on the first (or last) page of all page groups. [pagegroups_overview.pdf, Page 1]
- **White-space-based page groups** — page groups are created when white space (or IOCA image data) is found in an area. [creatingpagegroupscontainer.pdf, Page 1]

You can also define **header and trailer pages** after creating page groups. [creatingpagegroupscontainer.pdf, Page 1]

After defining page groups and index tags in a sample AFP file using RICOH Visual Workbench, you must add a step to one or more workflows to apply those definitions to production AFP files. [indexingafpfiles.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| File Type | Tool to Use |
|-----------|-------------|
| **PDF** | RICOH ProcessDirector Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat |
| **AFP** | RICOH Visual Workbench (AFP Indexer) |
per_question.judge_rationale: Correctly identifies the Plug-in for Adobe Acrobat (Define Page Group) for PDF and AFP Indexer/Visual Workbench for AFP with well-cited evidence, but omits that page groups identify individual documents/mailpieces.

per_question.question: When setting up a workflow for the Advanced Transform feature that handles jobs in multiple datastream formats, what should I set the input stream property to?
per_question.answer:
## Setting the Input Stream Property for Multi-Format Workflows

When configuring a workflow for the Advanced Transform feature that handles jobs in multiple datastream formats, you should set the **Transform input stream** property to **"Use current"**.

### Why This Setting?

This setting is appropriate in two specific scenarios:

1. **When the workflow processes jobs in various datastreams** (multiple different input formats) [cpt_c_WorkflowsForAdvTransforms.pdf, Page 1]
2. **When jobs contain multiple data types**, such as AFP print jobs that include images or PDF files in object containers [cpt_c_WorkflowsForAdvTransforms.pdf, Page 1]

### How It Works

Setting **Transform input stream** to **"Use current"** causes the transform to use the value of the **Input data stream** property as the transform input stream [aiwctransjt.pdf, Page 1]. This is typically determined upstream in the workflow by a step based on the **DetectInputDatastream** step template, which detects and sets the Input data stream property for each job [aiwctransjt.pdf, Page 1].

### Step-by-Step Setup

1. Click the **Workflow** tab [cpt_c_WorkflowsForAdvTransforms.pdf, Page 1]

However, if the job then finishes within a **second (later) deadline**, the **Deadline outcome is reset to "Met"**, because:

The documentation provides a direct example of exactly this scenario:

> *"You set a deadline of 3:00 to finish the print step and 5:00 to finish an insertion step. At some point, a job misses the print deadline by 5 minutes, but it still meets the insertion deadline. **The final value of the Deadline outcome property is Met** even though a previous deadline (for print) was missed."* [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]

| Event | Deadline Outcome | Red Dot Status |
|---|---|---|
| Job misses first deadline | Missed | 🔴 Red dot appears |
| Job meets second deadline | **Reset to Met** | ✅ Red dot **cleared** |

So the red dot would **not remain** — once the job meets its subsequent deadline, the Deadline outcome is updated to **Met**, reflecting the most recent deadline result. [dt_c_settingdeadlines.pdf, Page 1]

per_question.question: When I install a new color conversion CMR using AFP Resource Installer, what does the software automatically do, and how does that help the printer?

## What AFP Resource Installer Automatically Does When You Install a New Color Conversion CMR

When you install a new color conversion CMR using AFP Resource Installer, the software performs the following automatic actions and provides the following benefits:

---

### 🔧 What the Software Automatically Does

**Step 1 – Automatic Creation of Link (LK) CMRs**

When you use AFP Resource Installer to install a color conversion CMR, the software **automatically creates link (LK) CMRs** between the new color conversion CMR and **every existing** color conversion CMR already in the resource library. [cac_ResInst.pdf, Page 1]

This same behavior applies in reverse: if you ever **uninstall** an audit or instruction color conversion CMR, AFP Resource Installer automatically **deletes** the corresponding link (LK) CMRs for every affected combination. [cac_CMRModeLink.pdf, Page 1]

**Step 2 – Automatic Download of Matching Link CMRs at Print Time**

When a print file references the new CMR, the print server **automatically downloads the link CMRs** that match the target device type and model, and sends them to the printer along with the print job. [cac_ResInst.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 🖨️ How This Helps the Printer

This process provides a significant performance benefit to the printer:

- **The printer can use the pre-built link (LK) CMR directly**, instead of having to spend extra time creating one itself during job processing. [cac_ResInst.pdf, Page 1]
- Without this automation, the printer would have to either:
  - **Create link (LK) CMRs on the fly** while processing print jobs, or
  - **Convert colors twice** — first from the original color space to the ICC Profile Connection Space (PCS), and then from the PCS to the printer's color space. [cac_CMRModeLink.pdf, Page 1]
- By having ready-made link CMRs available, the printer only needs to perform **one color conversion** instead of two, saving processing time and resources. [cac_CMRModeLink.pdf, Page 1]

---

### 📋 Summary Table

| Action | Who Does It | When |
|---|---|---|
| Creates LK CMRs for all audit/instruction combinations | AFP Resource Installer (automatically) | At CMR installation time |
| Downloads matching LK CMRs to the printer | Print server (automatically) | At print job submission time |
| Uses LK CMR for single-step color conversion | Printer | During print job processing |

per_question.question: When building widgets in Predictive Insight using Job Step Progress data, why would summing Cumulative pages stacked across all steps give wrong totals, and how do you fix it?

## Why Summing Cumulative Pages Stacked Across All Steps Gives Wrong Totals — and How to Fix It

---

### The Root Cause

The problem stems from how the **Job Step Progress data collector** records data in the `job_history` table.

The data collector records an entry **at the beginning and end of each step** in the workflow. Because of this, properties like **Cumulative pages stacked** and **Cumulative sheets stacked** appear in **multiple rows** — one for each step [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1].

Critically, these cumulative values **do not change from step to step** after the PrintJobs step. The same value is simply repeated in every subsequent row. The value only updates if the job passes through the PrintJobs step again (e.g., for a reprint) [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1].

So if your widget sums **Cumulative pages stacked** across all steps for a job, RICOH Predictive Insight will **add together all those repeated identical values**, producing a total that is a multiple of the real figure — which is **incorrect** [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1].

---

### How to Fix It

The documentation gives the following clear guidance:

> *"To include one of those values in a widget, be sure that you do not include the values from multiple steps. RICOH Predictive Insight will add the values together and therefore provide incorrect results."*
> [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1]

To correct this, follow these steps:

1. **Download and examine the CSV file** for the Job Step Progress data collector first, so you can see exactly how the data repeats row by row across steps [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1].

2. **Use a formula or filter** in your widget to ensure that only **one row per job** is included in the calculation — specifically, the row from a single, well-defined step (e.g., the row recorded at the end of the PrintJobs step) [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1].

3. **Apply a widget filter** to restrict the data to that single step, preventing RICOH Predictive Insight from summing the duplicated values across all steps [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1].

---

### Summary Table

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Totals are too high | Same cumulative value repeated in every post-print step row | Filter or formula to include only one row per job |
| N/A values in chart | Some steps have no value yet | Add a widget filter to exclude N/A rows [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1] |

---

**Key takeaway:** Always analyze the raw CSV data before building widgets, and never sum a cumulative property across all steps — use a filter or formula to isolate a single step's row [aiw_c_hintssupervisorconnect.pdf, Page 1].
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer closely tracks evidence [3] and conveys all three key facts; only minor unsupported embellishments (e.g., 'end of PrintJobs step' row example, 'multiple of the real figure') go slightly beyond the source.

per_question.question: When I shut down a Passthrough printer in RICOH ProcessDirector while a job is actively printing, what status does that job end up in?

When you shut down a **Passthrough printer** while a job is actively printing, the resulting job status depends on whether the printer command completed successfully before the shutdown was processed:

---

### Two Possible Outcomes:

1. **Status: `Complete`**
   - This occurs **if the printer command returned successfully** before the shutdown was processed. [aiw00pshutdown.pdf, Page 1]

2. **Status: `Error`**
   - This occurs **if the printer command did NOT return successfully** before the shutdown was processed. [aiw00pshutdown.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Condition | Resulting Job Status |
|---|---|
| Printer command returned successfully before shutdown | **Complete** |
| Printer command did NOT return successfully before shutdown | **Error** |

---

- Once the shutdown is executed, the printer is **disabled**, meaning no further jobs can print on it until it is re-enabled, and RICOH ProcessDirector cannot schedule new jobs to it. [aiw00pshutdown.pdf, Page 1]
- Note that this behavior is **specific to Passthrough printers** (as well as PCLOut, Kodak PDF, and Xerox PDF printers). Other printer types, such as Ricoh PDF or AFP printers, follow different status transition rules. [aiw00pshutdown.pdf, Page 1]

per_question.question: If a PDF 2.0 file goes through a workflow where no steps modify the PDF, does it get converted to PDF 1.7, and what happens if banner pages are enabled when sending to a Ricoh PDF printer?

## PDF 2.0 Workflow Behavior and Banner Pages with Ricoh PDF Printers

### 1. What happens to a PDF 2.0 file if no workflow steps modify it?

If a PDF 2.0 file goes through a workflow where **no steps modify the PDF**, it will **not** be converted — it passes through RICOH ProcessDirector in **PDF 2.0 format** unchanged.

However, there is an important exception: if a **PDF 2.0 file** is sent to a **Ricoh PDF, TASKalfa, or Ricoh TotalFlow printer** with **banner pages turned on**, the file **will be converted to PDF 1.7 format**, because PDF 1.7 is required for the banner pages to function.

> *"If you print a PDF 2.0 file with banner pages, the file is converted to PDF 1.7 format which is required for the banner pages."* [aiw_ricohpdfptr_bannerpgs.pdf, Page 1]

> *"If you print a PDF 2.0 file with banner pages, the file is converted to PDF 1.7 format which is required for the banner pages."* [aiw_pdfbanners.pdf, Page 1]

|---|---|
| PDF 2.0 → workflow with **no modifying steps** | Stays as **PDF 2.0** [aiw00o2.pdf, Page 1] |
| PDF 2.0 → workflow with **steps that modify the PDF** | Converted to **PDF 1.7** [aiw00o2.pdf, Page 1] |

per_question.question: If I deactivate a custom property to change its settings and then reactivate it, do I need to manually re-add it to the objects it was previously connected to?
per_question.answer:
## Re-adding Custom Properties After Reactivation

**Yes, you will need to manually re-add the custom property to all objects it was previously connected to.** Here is a detailed explanation of what happens during the deactivation/reactivation cycle:

---

### What Happens When You Deactivate a Custom Property

When a custom property is deactivated, the following occurs:

- **All connections to any objects where the custom property was added are lost.** The custom property is removed from any objects it was previously connected to. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]
- Any commands or processes based on the custom property might not function properly. For example, **connector rules that use the property will fail to evaluate correctly.** [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]

---

### What Happens When You Reactivate a Custom Property

When the custom property is reactivated:

- **The property is NOT automatically added back** to the jobs or objects it was removed from. You must manually reconnect it. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]
- Processes and commands that include the property **should start to function correctly again** once reactivated. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]
- You will need to **add the custom property back to all the objects it was removed from.** [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Recommended Steps When Reactivating

After making your configuration changes and reactivating the property, Ricoh recommends the following procedure:

1. **Log out** of RICOH ProcessDirector. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]
2. **Refresh the browser window** and clear your browser cache. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]
3. **Log back in** to RICOH ProcessDirector. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]
4. **Manually re-add** the custom property to all objects it was previously connected to. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]

---

### ⚠️ Important Recommendation

To avoid this disruption, Ricoh strongly recommends **thoroughly testing** any new custom property in a small number of representative places before broad deployment, so that configuration changes requiring deactivation are minimized. [aiw_creating_customprop.pdf, Page 1]
per_question.judge_rationale: The answer accurately conveys all three key facts with correct citations; only minor embellishment in the closing testing recommendation framing.

per_question.question: If we add a color printing line using an InfoPrint 5000, can we still run those color jobs on our existing InfoPrint 4100 or InfoPrint 4000 printers as a fallback?
per_question.answer:
## Fallback Printing: InfoPrint 5000 Color Jobs on InfoPrint 4100 / InfoPrint 4000

Unfortunately, **no** — color jobs designed for the InfoPrint 5000 **cannot** be used as a fallback on your existing InfoPrint 4100 or InfoPrint 4000 printers.

The documentation is explicit on this point:

> *"Those print jobs cannot be run on the existing InfoPrint 4100 or InfoPrint 4000 printers, since those printers cannot print the required color elements."*
> [cac_ReplacePrintedForms.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Why is this the case?

- The **InfoPrint 5000** is a full-color, high-speed continuous forms IPDS printer with full AFP color management support, using piezo-electric inkjet technology with color pigment inks. [cac_IP5000.pdf, Page 1]
- The **InfoPrint 4100**, even with the InfoPrint POWER architecture and microcode release 15.4 or later, only supports **high-quality grayscale** printing — it cannot reproduce the full color elements required by InfoPrint 5000 color workflows. [cac_IP4100.pdf, Page 1]
- The **InfoPrint 4000** has no AFP color management support referenced in the evidence at all. [cac_Printers.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Recommended Path Forward

While a direct color fallback is not possible, there **is** a productive intermediate step you can take:

1. **Migrate applications to high-quality grayscale** on your InfoPrint 4100 printers by upgrading to microcode release 15.4 or later and installing the AFP Color Emulation feature. [cac_ReplacePrintedForms.pdf, Page 1]
2. Use **AFP Resource Installer** to manage images and associate them with the correct halftones and tone transfer curves for the best grayscale output quality. [cac_Halftone_4100.pdf, Page 1]
3. As your team becomes proficient and your business case grows, you can **add additional InfoPrint 5000 color lines** — either by reducing paper storage needs or by replacing InfoPrint 4000 lines — and then migrate those grayscale-ready jobs to full color. [cac_ReplacePrintedForms.pdf, Page 1]

---

### Summary Table

| Printer | Full Color | High-Quality Grayscale | Fallback for IP5000 Color Jobs |
|---|---|---|---|
| InfoPrint 5000 | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | N/A |
| InfoPrint 4100 (microcode 15.4+) | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ❌ **No** |
| InfoPrint 4000 | ❌ No | ❌ No | ❌ **No** |

[cac_ReplacePrintedForms.pdf, Page 1] [cac_Printers.pdf, Page 1] [cac_IP4100.pdf, Page 1]
